steps.title: Prepare required solutions
steps.instruction: Make all buffers the day before (or as noted) using the exact quantities:

substeps.instruction: 1× PBS (100 mL): mix 10 mL 10× PBS with 900 mL deionized water; store at 4 °C.
Subbing solution for slides (1 L): dissolve 1 g gelatin in hot distilled water, cool, add 0.1 g chromium potassium sulfate; submerge slides, store aliquots at 4 °C.
2.5 % normal horse serum blocking buffer (3 mL): combine 75 µL normal horse serum with 2 925 µL 1× PBS; store at 4 °C.
3 % hydrogen peroxide (1 mL): mix 30 µL 30 % H₂O₂ with 970 µL 1× PBS; store at 4 °C.
Ice‑cold acetone fixative (1 mL): place 1 mL acetone on ice; store at –20 °C.
10 mM DAPI stock (50 mL): dissolve 35 µL of 14.3 mM DAPI in 49.955 µL deionized water, bring to 50 mL with water; store at 4 °C protected from light.

steps.title: Prepare embedding reagents and mount
steps.instruction: Set up the freezing and mounting apparatus before the biopsy:

substeps.instruction: Place a 5‑inch circular Styrofoam cryo‑dewar filled with liquid nitrogen.
In a 20 mL beaker, combine ~100–150 µg gum tragacanth with 3–4 drops deionized water; stir with a spatula.
Add an equal volume of OCT compound (1:1 ratio) to form a thick paste.
Pour 10 mL 2‑methylbutane (isopentane) into a 125 mL stainless‑steel container.
Cut a size‑zero stopper cork in half; drill a central channel with a #11 scalpel to create a platform; attach the larger half to the scalpel handle for later handling.

steps.title: Embed muscle biopsy in OCT
steps.instruction: Within 20 min of tissue extraction, embed the sample while keeping it frozen:

substeps.instruction: Place the freshly obtained 150–300 mg vastus lateralis biopsy on a sterile 100 mm Petri dish, trim excess connective tissue, and rinse with 1× PBS if heavily blood‑stained.
Using a sterile scalpel, cut the specimen to ~0.5–0.75 cm length (≈25–100 mg tissue) to retain intact fibers.
Position the stainless‑steel isopentane container in the liquid‑nitrogen dewar and wait until isopentane begins to crystallize (white solids at the bottom).
Under a stereomicroscope, orient the cut fibers parallel to the long axis of the cork platform.
Place the tissue upright on the cork, gently work the OCT‑gum paste around it to eliminate air gaps, then add a thin OCT cover layer.
When isopentane is solidifying, flip the cork upside‑down and immerse it fully in the liquid‑nitrogen‑cooled isopentane for ~30 s until the OCT hardens.
Detach the embedded block, place it on aluminum foil atop a plastic Petri dish floating above liquid nitrogen for 60 min to allow controlled freezing.
Store the block at –80 °C for long‑term (up to 2 years) or at –20 °C for short‑term (up to 6 months) until sectioning.

steps.title: Section tissue with cryostat
steps.instruction: Cut 20 µm sections and collect them on subbed slides:

substeps.instruction: Set cryostat temperature to –23 °C and stage‑knife angle to 4° (other labs use 8–10°).
Label each Superfrost Plus slide with subject ID, slide number, antibodies, stains, date, and initials.
Transfer the frozen block quickly to the cryostat chamber, keeping it frozen.
Apply a thin layer of OCT to the chuck stub, embed the block flat and perpendicular to the knife, and spray cold air to solidify the OCT.
Mount the chuck in the holder, align the block perpendicular to the blade, and install the appropriate microtome blade.
Trim the block face (facing) until tissue is visible.
Collect sections in an alternating 20 µm → trash → collect pattern, placing ~3 sections per slide, centered away from edges; use a camel‑hair brush if sections roll.
Dry slides at room temperature for 30 min; proceed immediately to staining (do not store overnight to avoid autofluorescence).

steps.title: Day 1: Fix, block, and add primary
steps.instruction: Perform fixation, peroxidase quenching, blocking, and primary antibody incubation in a humid chamber:

substeps.instruction: Place slides in a plastic humidity chamber with a moist paper towel to prevent evaporation.
Fix sections in ice‑cold acetone: pipette 75 µL acetone onto each section, incubate 3 min on ice, then discard.
Wash sections 3 × 3 min with 1× PBS (use a beaker of PBS to avoid contamination).
Add 75 µL 3 % H₂O₂ in 1× PBS to each section; incubate 7 min at room temperature (RT). Bubbles indicate activity.
Wash sections 3 × 3 min with 1× PBS.
Block with 75 µL 2.5 % normal horse serum (blocking buffer); incubate 60 min at RT.
Prepare primary antibody cocktails (all diluted in 2.5 % NHS):
– Slides 1 & 2 (6 sections total): 500 µL of Pax7 (1:100) + laminin (1:200).
– Slide 3 (3 sections): 300 µL Pax7 (1:100).
– Slide 4 (3 sections): 300 µL laminin (1:200).
Add 75 µL of the appropriate primary cocktail to each section; incubate overnight at 4 °C in the dark.

steps.title: Day 2: Secondary staining and mounting
steps.instruction: Apply secondary antibodies, tyramide amplification, DAPI, and mount the slides:

substeps.instruction: Wash slides 4 × 5 min with 1× PBS.
Pax7 secondary (slides 1‑3): add 75 µL goat anti‑mouse IgG1 biotin (1:1,000) in 2.5 % NHS; incubate 1 h at RT in the dark (foil‑covered). Leave slide 4 in PBS.
Wash slides 4 × 5 min with 1× PBS.
Laminin secondary (slides 1, 2, 4): add 75 µL mixture of goat anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200) plus streptavidin‑HRP (1:100) in 1× PBS; incubate 1 h at RT in the dark. Leave slide 3 in PBS.
Wash slides 3 × 5 min with 1× PBS.
Tyramide signal amplification (slides 1‑4): add 75 µL Alexa Fluor 594 tyramide (1:200) in 1× PBS; incubate 20 min at RT in the dark.
Wash slides 3 × 5 min with 1× PBS.
DAPI counterstain: add 75 µL 10 mM DAPI; incubate 30 min at RT (or overnight at 4 °C). If overnight, wash 5 × 5 min PBS the next day.
Wash slides 3 × 5 min with 1× PBS.

Mounting: cut the tip off a 200 µL pipette tip, place 3–4 droplets (20–50 µL total) of Vectashield antifade medium on each slide, lower a 22 × 50 mm No. 1.5 coverslip, avoid bubbles, let spread 1–2 min.
Seal edges with nail polish, store slides in a slide holder at 4 °C in the dark until imaging.

steps.title: Acquire confocal Z‑stack images
steps.instruction: Capture multichannel 3‑D images on the Leica TCS SPE confocal microscope:

substeps.instruction: Turn on laser lines (405, 488, 561, 635 nm), microscope controller, and white light source.
Launch LAS X software, load the slide, and locate the region with a low‑magnification objective (10×/20×).
Select the TXR (561 nm) channel to locate Pax7‑positive cells; confirm overlap with DAPI (405 nm) and laminin (488 nm) signals.
Switch to a higher magnification oil‑immersion objective (40×/1.15 NA) using Type F immersion liquid (catalog 11513859).
Set three sequential channels:
– DAPI: 405 nm excitation, emission 430–480 nm, adjust laser intensity/gain to reach ~60 % histogram, pseudo‑color blue.
– Laminin (GFP/FITC): 488 nm excitation, emission 500–540 nm, pseudo‑color green.
– Pax7 (TXR): 561 nm excitation, emission 600–640 nm, pseudo‑color red.
Select low‑pixel resolution (512 × 512) live mode to define region of interest.
Determine Z‑stack range by moving the objective until signal disappears in both directions; set start and end positions.
Set final acquisition parameters: pixel resolution 1 024 × 1 024, Z‑step 0.44 µm (total Z ≈ 19.49 µm), scan speed 400 µs/pixel, pinhole 1 AU, image size 275 µm, pixel size 268.82 nm, zoom factor 1.0.
Start acquisition and record all settings (z‑step, laser power, gain, pinhole, etc.).

steps.title: Process images in 3D Viewer
steps.instruction: Render and export the 3‑D stacks using LAS X 3D Viewer:

substeps.instruction: Open the acquired image file in 3D Viewer, set background to black, and choose Overlay under the Volume tab.
Adjust each channel histogram (DAPI, Pax7, laminin) to similar ranges (e.g., low ≈ 3, high ≈ 250) while keeping gamma at 1.0.
Set overall intensity to 100 and fine‑tune if needed to match brightness across samples.
Navigate with mouse rotation, x‑y translation, and zoom to the desired view; note the zoom percentage.
Add a scale bar (Times New Roman, font size 26) if desired.
Save the final visualization as a TIFF file (e.g., 1 024 × 1 024 pixels).
